claims.claim_summary: OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/32 zero-shot accuracy varies substantially across five standard domains (42.45% to 85.06%), with severe class-level failures (including 0% classes) persisting even in high-accuracy datasets.
claims.controls: Frozen OpenAI ViT-B/32 checkpoint, FP32, QuickGELU, fixed single prompt per dataset without test-set tuning.
claims.uncertainty: Full official test splits evaluated deterministically; per-class support documented in reports/baseline/per_class.csv.
limitations: Cross-dataset accuracy differences reflect domain, candidate count, and class naming, not model improvements.
DTD uses test partition 1 only, not the 10-partition average.

claims.claim_summary: On 1,080 synthetic counting scenes, accuracy is 32.87% (above 16.67% chance, MAE 1.0157), remains low (34.45%) on the 74.44% subset where color/shape recognition succeeds, and is similar between fixed radius (32.41%) and fixed total area (33.33%).
limitations: Synthetic 2D shapes differ from natural images.
Accuracy across counts 1-6 is non-monotonic (52.22% at count 3 vs 9.44% at count 4); do not claim a monotonic degradation law.

claims.claim_summary: On 720 synthetic two-object scenes (1,440 trials), CLIP achieves 86.11% accuracy without affirmative bias (48.06% affirmative choices), but shows a 10.56 percentage-point sensitivity between 'with/without' (91.39%) and 'contains/does not contain' (80.83%), with 58.61% full-group consistency.
limitations: Do not claim 'CLIP fails at negation' from this study; in this controlled 2-object geometric setup, accuracy is 86.11%.
Does not cover cluttered natural scenes with multiple distractors.

claims.topic: Fine-grained classification and within-superclass oracle diagnostic
claims.claim_summary: Restricting CIFAR-100 candidates to the 5 true coarse-group classes (oracle 5-way) yields 77.95% accuracy (2,205 within-group errors remain), while full candidate-set evaluation across Pet, Flowers102, DTD, and Food-101 reveals systematic confusions between visually or lexically similar classes.
claims.controls: Exact 10,000/10,000 global prediction parity against baseline CIFAR-100 run.
limitations: 77.95% uses ground-truth coarse labels (oracle) and must never be presented as a deployable improvement over 64.48% 100-way accuracy.

claims.claim_summary: Across 1,440 synthetic scenes and 8,640 trials, object recognition reaches 96.94% but 4-way spatial classification is 27.36% (T0 forward), with strong bias toward 'above' (56.18%), 0.56% horizontal pair consistency, 0% all-four-relation consistency, and 16.25% agreement between grammatically equivalent forward/reversed prompts.
claims.controls: Two-object recognition control (96.94%) and blank-canvas prior check (23.82% agreement).
limitations: Blank-canvas predictions agree with only 23.82% of scene predictions, ruling out a pure image-ignoring constant prior.
Behavioral probe does not isolate specific internal transformer layers or attention heads.

claims.topic: Controlled category prompt study on CIFAR-100
claims.claim_summary: Appending the true coarse category ('a photo of a {class}, a type of {category}.') outperforms five deranged wrong-category mappings by +8.734 percentage points, but reduces Top-1 accuracy by 1.56 percentage points relative to baseline (62.92% vs 64.48%) and by 1.17 percentage points relative to token-length-matched neutral suffixes (64.09%), because strongest rival scores increase more than target class scores.
claims.controls: Token-length-matched neutral suffixes (exact token match in 80/100 classes, +/-1 token in 20 classes) and 5 derangement permutations (seeds 271-275).
limitations: Evaluated on the CIFAR-100 test split for a single category template structure prior to P3 multi-template expansion.
Strongest rival changes identity in 33.75% of images; fixed baseline rival score delta is -0.000111.

claims.topic: Natural-image spatial probing and preregistered 2x2 confirmation on COCO val2014
claims.claim_summary: On 200 screened COCO val2014 images, 4-way spatial accuracy (T2 forward) is 28.00% (28.41% on 176 retained after second review) with a 62.00% 'right' prediction bias; on a frozen confirmation set of 100 new horizontal sources disjoint from all 400 prior candidates, 2x2 debiased assignment accuracy is 53.00% (53/100, p = 0.3086 vs 50%), while only 4.00% of original/mirror pairs are both individually correct.
claims.controls: Source ID disjointness against all 400 previously screened candidates, 64-bit dHash screening, selection freeze timestamp prior to inference, and 2x2 assignment gap cancelling additive per-image/per-caption biases.
limitations: Non-significant p = 0.3086 does not prove p = 0.50 or zero spatial information.
Visual screening was performed by the same AI assistant + geometric validator, without independent human annotators.
No separate object-recognition control has yet been run on the COCO subset (planned as diagnostic option P2.1).
